identity.title: A Surface Density Perturbation in the TW Hydrae Disk at 95 au Traced by Molecular Emission

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present ALMA Cycle 2 observations at $0.5\ensuremath{''}$ resolution of TW Hya of CS $J=5-4$ emission.

evidence.quote: TW Hya, as the nearest protoplanetary disk to us at $59\pm1$ pc (cite: Gaia_2016)

question.value: Is the dip in the CS J=5-4 radial profile at 1.6'' in TW Hya caused by a gas surface density perturbation (as in scattered light) rather than a chemical or dust-only effect?

evidence.quote: we follow the modelling carried out by (cite: vanBoekel_ea_2016) and argue that these features are the product of a depression in the surface density of the gas rather than a chemical effect.
The ALMA Cycle 2 observations, project 2013.1.00387.S, were performed on May 13, 2015.

findings_qualitative.value: A 55% surface density depression (Model C) gives the best match to the CS dip; a 30% depression has no effect; a full gap is too deep; dust-only perturbations give CS enhancement, contrary to observations.

evidence.quote: produces the best fit to the morphology of the radial profile.

findings_qualitative.value: The outer enhancement at ~3'' arises from the exponential surface density edge and increased UV penetration.

evidence.quote: naturally reproduce the outer enhancement at $3\ensuremath{''}$.

claims.hypothesis: A gas surface density perturbation explains the CS dip at 1.6''
claims.experiment: Thermochemical, chemical and non-LTE modelling of perturbed disks with simulated observations
claims.result: Model C (d=0.55) reproduces dip morphology; B too weak, D too deep
claims.finding: Surface density depression is consistent with the CS feature and scattered light

evidence.quote: Model C clearly has a radial morphology which is comparable to the observations while Model Cd lacks the depression at $1.6\ensuremath{''}$.

claims.hypothesis: A dust-only gap could produce the CS feature
claims.experiment: Models Bd, Cd, Dd with only dust surface density perturbed
claims.result: Enhanced gas-to-dust ratio reduces freeze-out and enhances CS
claims.finding: Dust-only gap cannot reproduce the feature

evidence.quote: resulting in an enhancement of CS emission, in clear contrast to the observations.

claims.hypothesis: The outer CS enhancement at 3.1'' has a chemical origin
claims.experiment: UV flux analysis in the models
claims.result: Reproduced in all models, tied to the exponential edge
claims.finding: Likely enhanced UV penetration and desorption, though not proven for TW Hya

evidence.quote: we cannot make such a claim for TW Hya.

why_this_method.value: Molecular emission depends on both excitation and abundance, so self-consistent modelling is needed

evidence.quote: it is important to perform self-consistent modelling taking into account the impact of the surface density perturbations on the physical structure and the resulting change in chemical abundances.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Instabilities producing azimuthal structure are disfavoured given no azimuthal variance; MRI dead-zone edge and grain evolution remain candidates

evidence.quote: instabilities which routinely produce vortices, spiral arms or azimuthally asymmetric gaps are likely not present at $\sim 90$ au in TW Hya.

limitations_admitted.value: Models do not fully reproduce observed profiles; fiducial model was fit to integrated intensities

evidence.quote: Clearly these models do not fully recover the observations profiles of TW Hya

referee_caveats_inferred: Model-observation comparison is qualitative with no fit or statistical test
Model intensities off by factor ~2 in the inner disk
Dip vs bump degeneracy due to lack of baseline
Single fiducial model; alternatives like grain evolution not modelled
